notes: Controlled vocabularies. Every facet value in data/ must appear here; `crafterwiki validate` enforces it. Add values here first, with a definition, before using them in a record.

placement_status.definition: Overall 1st place, or the only prize of the event.
Won a named track, category or sponsor prize.
Named runner-up of a track or prize by the organizer.
Selected into the organizer's finalist round.
Ranked by a public/community vote. Store rank and votes. Not a jury result.
Showcased by the organizer without a stated placement.
Win claimed by a team member or secondary source; official results not retrieved. Must carry a verification note.
Appears on a submission or voting list; no placement known. Used for base rates and saturation, never as a winner.

analysis_basis.definition: The organizer or judges wrote it (results post, judge comment, prize citation).
The team wrote it (Devpost story, README, interview).
CrafterWIKI's own reading of the evidence. Must be labelled as such in every surface.

domains.definition: Securing AI agents, models, prompts, data leakage to AI.
Gateways, registries, identity, orchestration and tooling for AI agents (MCP, A2A).
Agents that pay, get paid, negotiate or hold money.
Personal/business finance, credit, investing, payments for humans.
Public procurement, public records, corruption risk, civic oversight.
Access to justice, compliance, regulation, legal documents.
Medical, clinical, wellbeing, rehab.
Disaster response, rescue, emergency comms and dispatch.
Products for people with disabilities.
Learning, tutoring, test prep, curriculum.
Job search, interviews, hiring, talent matching.
Climate, energy, waste, sustainable systems.
Games, play, fun, music-as-play.
Art, music, video, 3D and content generation.
Tools for software developers.
Kubernetes, cloud cost, platform engineering.
Personal/team productivity and assistants.
Relationships, community, social experiences.
Personal memory, journaling, nostalgia, reminiscence.
Shopping, marketplaces, merchants, pricing.
Simulating futures, policies, risks or populations.
Identity, authenticity, content provenance, human verification.
Turning web/docs into structured data or APIs.
Physical devices, robots, embedded systems as the core product.
Network security, OSINT, forensics (non-AI-specific).
Property search and transactions.
Marketing, go-to-market, sponsorships, advertising.
Screening companies/people, KYC, risk files.
Satellite and Earth-science data applied to weather, land, water, vegetation or air.
Astrophysics, heliophysics, planetary science, exoplanets, space biology.
Orbits, debris, satellites, habitats, missions and the space economy.
Farming, crops, food systems, rural livelihoods.
Internet access, networks, satellite and radio communications.

mechanisms.definition: The team designed the demo moment first; judges get a 'wait, it does that?' reaction.
The demo does the real thing live in the room, not canned data.
Hardware or a physical prop on the judging table carries the first impression.
The idea can be repeated by a judge in one sentence.
An object or app everyone knows is given a job it was never meant for.
Flips the standard approach or serves the side of the market everyone ignores.
A specific person with a real consequence is on the other side of the product.
A genuinely hard technical problem is solved and shown, not just claimed.
Small scope that fully works end to end.
One engine serves two audiences or business models.
Outputs carry sources, dates and self-limiting explanations; trust is a feature.
Deep, idiomatic use of the required or sponsor platform.
Rides a channel users already have (FaceTime, WhatsApp, Telegram, browser).
Does cheaply or in a weekend what normally costs a lot.
Answers the event theme with a clever, non-literal interpretation.
Rides the technology wave judges and sponsors care about that season.
Does not stop at a report: drafts the request, opens the PR, moves the robot.
Video, write-up/blog and repo are all strong; matters most in online judging.
The submission is merged upstream work.
Borrows a beloved cultural reference (Iron Man's DUM-E, Bob Ross, Furby, a Nerf gun) so judges get it instantly.
Makes an invisible infrastructure capability tangible by wrapping it in a familiar app scenario.
Turns data only experts can read (mission, satellite, lab) into something a non-expert can explore, feel or act on.
Anchored in one named place and its people (a city, a forest, a region), so the impact is concrete and checkable.

judging_lenses.definition: Stands out and leaves a lasting impression.
Intuitive, polished, engaging for its audience.
Real-world or social impact, practical utility.
Growth potential, unique insight, could become a company.
Creative and effective use of a sponsor's platform.
Team development practices, code quality, incremental delivery.
Decided by community voting; distribution and pitch reach matter.
Narrative, pitch delivery and demo storyline.
Scientifically sound; would do what it claims in the real world (NASA Space Apps 'Validity').
Answers the stated challenge; complete, feasible and usable (NASA Space Apps 'Relevance').

ai_patterns.definition: Calls a hosted LLM for generation or analysis.
Exposes or federates an MCP server.
Detection, segmentation, pose, face or gesture tracking.
Agent operates a desktop or browser.
LLM used to grade or score human output.
Trains or runs a non-LLM machine-learning model (classifier, detector, forecaster, optimizer).
The source says AI is used without saying how. Do not upgrade to a specific pattern without evidence.

build_styles.definition: A mission or system concept with models and analysis rather than a working product.
A story, illustration, game or other media artifact is the deliverable.

event_kinds.definition: Large student hackathon (MLH-style), many sponsor prizes.
Run by an accelerator/VC; startup-shaped problems.
Run by a company to showcase its platform/API.
Run around open-source projects; contributions count.
Short community hackathon or build night.
Run by a public agency around its open data: hundreds of local events, global multi-phase judging by subject-matter experts (e.g. NASA Space Apps).

results_status.definition: Only a community vote ranking is known.
Only the submission list is known.

roster_coverage.definition: Every submission of the event is indexed; track/domain counts are valid base rates.
Some non-placing submissions are indexed; counts are NOT base rates.
Only placed projects are indexed; no saturation signal.

source_kinds.definition: Organizer results page or winners post.
Team-written project page on an organizer platform other than Devpost (e.g. Space Apps team pages).
Conversation with a participant; private, anonymized.
